links.note: Gabriel announces to Elizabeth that she will shortly bear a son to be named John, the forerunner.
Gabriel appears to Mary with glad tidings that her conception is ordained by heaven.
A celestial messenger appears to Joseph in a dream concerning the son Mary shall bear.
John is born to Zacharias and Elizabeth; the UB dates it March 25, 7 B.C.
Jesus is born, wrapped in clothes Mary brought, and laid in a manger.
The UB tells how the overcrowded inn led Joseph to lodgings in the caravan stables below it.
On the eighth day he is circumcised and formally named Joshua, which in English is called Jesus.
The UB states no shepherds or other mortals came to pay homage; only seraphim sang over the manger, unheard by human ears, until priests from Ur arrived.
Three teachers from Mesopotamia (priests of Ur) find the child and present gifts.
The UB states the wise men saw no star; the legend grew from a Jupiter-Saturn conjunction in 7 B.C.
Warned by a celestial message delivered through Zacharias, Joseph and Mary leave Bethlehem by night for Alexandria in Egypt.
Herod orders the slaughter of boy babies under two in Bethlehem.
Mary and Joseph bring the child to Jerusalem for the purification and presentation.
Jesus is baptized by John at the very height of John's preaching.
The UB identifies the voice from heaven as that of Jesus' Personalized Adjuster, speaking for the Universal Father.
The UB dates the baptism when Jesus was nearly thirty-one and one-half, and reconciles Luke's Tiberius reckoning with the co-regency with Augustus.
The UB places the great temptation on Mount Hermon before the baptism, not after.
The UB states Jesus did not fast or afflict his soul in the wilderness; he was not an ascetic.
Six stone waterpots, holding about twenty gallons apiece, stand near at hand at Cana.
The UB states Jesus was the most surprised person present and calls the wine-making 'in no sense a miracle': celestial personalities assembled the elements, abrogating time.
'Except a man be born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God.'
'Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again, but whosoever drinks of the water of the living spirit shall never thirst.'
Jesus gives thanks, breaks the bread, and distributes it to feed the multitude.
The UB presents the walking on the sea as Simon Peter's night vision in a dream, which he ever after believed was real.
'Hanker not after the meat which perishes but rather seek for the spiritual food that never fails.'
'I am this bread of life.'
'Today has salvation come to this home.'
The rich young man Matadormus asks Jesus what he must do to gain eternal life.
He goes away sorrowful, for he had great possessions.
'Happy are the poor in spirit, the humble, for theirs are the treasures of the kingdom of heaven.' The UB places the beatitudes in the ordination charge rather than the Sermon on the Mount.
'You are the salt of the earth, salt with a saving savor.'
'You are the light of the world. A city set upon a hill cannot be hid.'
The Believer's Prayer opens 'Our Father who is in heaven, hallowed be your name.'
'Give us this day our bread for tomorrow' — the UB's form of 'daily bread.'
'Forgive us every one our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.'
A lawyer asks, 'Who is my neighbor?' hoping to justify himself.
Jesus tells of a man going down from Jerusalem to Jericho who falls among cruel brigands.
'A certain man had two sons' — the UB's 'Parable of the Lost Son.'
The father calls for the best robe and the fatted calf for the returned son.
'I am both the door to the Father's sheepfold and the true shepherd of my Father's flocks.'
'I am the true shepherd who is willing even to lay down his life for the sheep.'
'I have many other sheep not of this fold' — the UB extends this to other worlds.
'I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.'
'I am the vine, and you are the branches' — expanded into the farewell discourse on fruit-bearing.
'Love one another, even as I have loved you' — the new commandment.
The UB presents the promised Comforter as the Spirit of Truth, soon to be sent to live in believers.
'If the Master has washed your feet, why were you unwilling to wash one another's feet?'
Mary anoints Jesus' head and feet with costly ointment and wipes his feet with her hair.
'Let her alone... she has done a good thing in her heart.'
The Alpheus twins put their cloaks on the donkey for the Master to ride.
Beholding Jerusalem, Jesus weeps over the city.
Jesus drives the animals from the temple and overturns the money-changers' tables; the UB narrates the cleansing without recording the 'den of thieves' saying.
Jesus' face and form shine with heavenly luminosity before the three apostles.
Peter 'erroneously conjectured' the two beings were Moses and Elijah; the UB states they were Gabriel and the Father Melchizedek.
A silvery cloud overshadows them.
'As often as you do this, do it in remembrance of me.'
The UB's cup words differ: 'the cup of my remembrance... the emblem of the bestowal and ministry of the divine Spirit of Truth' — not 'my blood.'
The UB's bread words differ: 'the bread of remembrance... the word of the Father, as revealed in the Son, is indeed the bread of life' — not 'my body.'
'What! can you not watch with me even for one hour?'
'The spirit is indeed willing, but the flesh is weak.'
'Not my will, but yours, be done.'
To 'Whom do you seek?' Jesus answers, 'I am he.'
Judas steps up, kisses his brow, and says, 'Hail, Master and Teacher.'
'Friend, is it not enough to do this! Would you even betray the Son of Man with a kiss?'
Peter stands with the attendants and warms himself at the charcoal fire in the courtyard.
'Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do' — spoken as they nailed him to the crossbeam.
The repentant brigand hears the promise that they shall 'sometime meet in Paradise.'
'Woman, behold your son!' — 'My son, behold your mother!'
'It is finished! Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.'
The final committal of his spirit; the UB joins both Gospel sayings in one paragraph.
The centurion: 'This was indeed a righteous man; truly he must have been a Son of God.'
The UB affirms the tomb was truly empty but states the material body was not resurrected; Jesus rose in morontia form.
The UB explains the resurrection form: not a spirit, but 'the very likeness of the morontia personalities.'
Appearing in the upper chamber: 'Peace be upon you.'
'As the Father sent me into the world, so send I you.'
'You will presently go into all the world preaching this gospel of the kingdom.'
'Tarry here in Jerusalem until I send you the Spirit of Truth... power from on high.'
'You will receive spiritual power after the spirit has descended upon you.'

note: Seed links curated and individually verified against the actual text of both sources on 2026-09-30. Relationship types: restates (same event/saying in both), expands (UB gives more detail), corrects (accounts differ; both texts shown, no editorializing), fulfills (UB presents itself as the fuller revelation of the theme).
